<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class), getMetaItemLayered (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via getPublished (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getPublished, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/published; the bare tail of client method meta.getPublished, bound to GET /meta/:type/:name/published))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via /:type/:name/published (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItemLayered — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **33** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `159648dc7ee6143d8e281ddd8fa2ff684b80545a` — the merge of head `678d6d6efecaff6645b7a0692548b2c13a3dacb6` into base `7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 159648dc7ee6143d8e281ddd8fa2ff684b80545a && git checkout 159648dc7ee6143d8e281ddd8fa2ff684b80545a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544 678d6d6efecaff6645b7a0692548b2c13a3dacb6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544 && git merge --no-ff 678d6d6efecaff6645b7a0692548b2c13a3dacb6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The central question: no served answer changes.** `appOf(packageId)` is `return packageId;` — a pure function of one string, no registry read, no manifest read, no environment or option, so on `main` it is the identity for every input and cannot be anything else. `pairOf(base)` is `customizationPackageId(…)` over `appOf(base)` when `base` is a non-empty string and over `base` itself otherwise: a non-empty string reaches the id rule unchanged; `undefined`, `''`, a number or any other value reaches it as itself and is refused `base_id_missing` exactly as before; a `.custom` id reaches it as itself and is refused `base_is_customization_package`; an id whose pair fails `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` is refused `base_id_invalid`. So `pairOf` ≡ `customizationPackageId` over the whole input domain, value and refusal reason alike. `isPairOf(pairId, base)` is `pair.ok && pair.value === pairId` over `pairOf(base)`, which is `isCustomizationPairOf`'s body over `customizationPackageId(baseId)` verbatim. Hence for every reachable input — an App package (`app.objectstack.hotcrm`), a module its artifact brings (`app.objectstack.hotcrm.service`, a real HotCRM id), a standalone package, a `sys` kernel package (`com.objectstack.plugin-auth`), a namespace-less manifest (the lookup never reads a namespace; the pair namespace is `customizationNamespace`'s, untouched) — the same pair id, the same refusal and the same predicate value as `main`. No new 200, no new pair id, no new namespace. TRUE.
- **The 20 class (i) sites moved only their call.** Every hunk in the 13 consumer files is one of: an import line (the spec helper removed, `pairOf` / `isPairOf` added to an existing or new `@objectstack/metadata-core` import), the one call `customizationPackageId(x)` → `pairOf(x)` with the same argument expression and the same guards around it, or a docblock sentence. Branches, refusal sentences, status codes, sort ranks (`protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts` 408/413), the `?package=` remedy text (`protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` 197/217), the uninstall refusal's `installedPair` (`registry.ts` 7315) and the `PackageUninstallExtendedError` shape are byte-identical. The dev's claim "nothing else in those functions moved" is TRUE.
- **The 3 `isCustomizationPairOf` sites.** `served-override.ts` 90 (`isServedOverrideRowOf`, the predicate five reads share), `protocol-class-head.ts` 191 (restore intent) and `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` 1075 (`judgeOverrideWrite`, which already reads `pairOf(base)` two lines up) now call `isPairOf`. Same arguments, same `unknown` tolerance. TRUE.
- **Census.** `git grep -n customizationPackageId origin/main -- 'packages/**/*.ts' ':!*.test.ts'` answers 53 lines in 17 files on today's `origin/main` as on `69e133ea` (the five line numbers I sampled at `69e133ea` match the body: discovery 330, write-gates 330, ensure door 255, runtime 669 / 3628, registry 7311). Per-file counts match the table; routed 20 + deferred 2 + stays 31 = 53; the diff's replacements count 20 `pairOf` + 3 `isPairOf`. The 31 stays are each an import (removed where the file no longer needs the spec helper), a docblock mention, the spec definition and its own inverse / predicate (5 + 1), the `PackageUninstallExtendedError.customizationPackageId` property declaration + assignment (a public error field, not a derivation), or lint 108, which reads only the `base_is_customization_package` refusal reason to skip a manifest that is itself a pair — a parse, and `packages/lint` does not declare `@objectstack/metadata-core`, so routing it would have added the edge the home was chosen to avoid. Classification holds. After the merge of `main` at `33bc8ae5f`, no new call site arrived (`git diff 33bc8ae5f origin/main` adds none). On the head the residual `customizationPackageId(` / `isCustomizationPairOf(` outside spec is the four lines the body names (the lookup, lint 108, runtime 672 / 3737) plus two docblock lines in the lookup. TRUE.
- **The runtime deferral.** `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` 672 (`customizeInPairRemedy`, a remedy sentence) and 3737 (`readPackageCustomizations`, the extensions read) are class (i) and left on `customizationPackageId`. Since `appOf` is the identity, both answer exactly as the routed sites do; nothing diverges until PR 2 moves `appOf`, which must route them then (the dev's out-of-scope note says so). The order allowed the deferral. One half of the stated reason has lapsed: PR #31008 merged at 2026-11-06T18:08Z and its merge commit is inside this head; #30756 (same seat) is still open on that file. Deferral stands; the body's sentence is half-stale (nit).
- **No `packages/spec` edit.** The 19-file list carries no `packages/spec/**` path; `customization-package.ts` and `package-lifecycle.zod.ts` keep every export. TRUE.
- **The home.** `@objectstack/metadata-core` declares `@objectstack/spec` and `zod` only, and its `src/` imports none of metadata-protocol, objectql, service-automation, service-datasource or runtime — no cycle. Each of the four consumers (and runtime) already declares `@objectstack/metadata-core: workspace:*`; `service-datasource` declares neither metadata-protocol nor objectql, which rules those two homes out. No `package.json` and no `pnpm-lock.yaml` in the diff. The new module imports `@objectstack/spec/kernel` only, no `import.meta`, no top-level side effect; `index.ts` adds one `export *`. TRUE.

That is a widening of the public face — see ② and should-fix 1.
- **Tests.** The new unit table (16 cases) pins, for the five shapes the order asked plus the module row, `appOf` = identity, `pairOf` = `customizationPackageId` = the literal pair, the five refusals through `pairOf`, and `isPairOf` = `isCustomizationPairOf` over seven candidates per row plus three edge cases. `tsconfig.json` `include: ['src/**/*']` reaches the test; `typecheck` runs both programs. The `.custom` refusal row pins that a pair id passed to `pairOf` still refuses — the pin PR 2's `appOf` must keep. The existing suites of every touched package are the behaviour pin (served rows, list and layered reads, write gates, uninstall refusal, flow remedy, import landing) and the diff touches none of them. No test on `main` mocks the seam (`vi.mock('@objectstack/spec/kernel')` occurs twice, overriding `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` and `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` only), so the routing is not observable to a mock either. (2) dist: `com.acme.crm → com.acme.suite`, metadata-core rebuilt, marker present in 2 built files → 48 metadata-protocol tests red across the served-override, pair-translation, named-base overlay write and packaged-base refusal suites, quoting the changed `?package=` remedy; restored, marker absent from 12 files, tree clean. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, accepted value, metadata type, default or meaning an author writes moves; every served `/meta` answer, refusal and pair id is identical. What the `yes` would owe — a review at least at `TIER_DEFAULT` — this record already exceeds, so nothing further is owed once the lines read `yes (widening)`. Check-runs on `979d839e` at 2026-11-06T18:41Z: 46 total, 21 success, 13 skipped, 12 in progress, 0 failed. Green: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Lint & Repo Gates` with every `Lint ·` leg (ESLint, repo & tooling gates, docs & code guards, CI/release & engine gates, PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped legs), `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Test UI`, `Plan Test Core shards`. In progress: `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1–8, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Live E2E UI`. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` — the one gate the dev could not measure (needs every package's dist) — runs inside `Build Core` (`ci.yml` 3083), so it is still unread; its risk is low (the new module has no `import.meta` and no side effect; the gate parses every emitted `.cjs` and requires the entry), but it is the gate this PR exists to pass and the seat reads it green before landing. ### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in 6692428237. The dev's out-of-scope note (runtime 672 / 3737 derive directly; the module row is the one PR 2 flips) is read and answered in ①.
- Deviations declared by the dev, all pre-agreed in amendment 6691222368: home `metadata-core`; the three `isCustomizationPairOf` sites (`served-override.ts` is not a `protocol-*.ts` file); harness assignee step skipped; `dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally; `patch` changeset, not `skip-changeset`. They answer the same as the server today and are not this PR's; under the App unit they become a second spelling that disagrees with the ensure door for a module package. Ruling 6691022506 already routes the console half to `domain:ui` (#29591 reads the served verdict); should-fix 2 asks that these six be named so PR 2's rehearsal does not meet them by surprise.
- Commits: four plus the merge; trailers `Co-Authored-By: Claude` + `Claude-Session`, no `Fixes`, no model name, no bare login. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The seam is in the right place and the right shape.** One function (`appOf`) carries the whole App-unit move; `pairOf` and `isPairOf` are the only two questions a caller asks, and the module doc forbids the direct spec call for "the pair of this package" while leaving the parse direction (`customizationBasePackageId`, `isCustomizationPackage`) with the spec. The residual-four sentence makes the rule checkable by `git grep` for PR 2's reviewer. The signature (`appOf(packageId: string): string`) is the one thing PR 2 will have to change — resolving a member to its App needs a manifest or registry read, which a pure function of the id cannot do — and the unit table's rows already carry `type`, `scope` and `namespace` for that day (nit 2). Holds.
- **The home holds against the dependency graph.** `metadata-core` is the lowest package all four callers already reach, it depends on none of them, and the two precedents the dev cites (the write dispatch predicates, the code-artifact provenance test) sank there for the same reason. Putting it in metadata-protocol would have forced service-datasource to declare a new edge; objectql likewise. Holds.
- **Readability.** No drive-by rename, no reformatting; the only prose changes are the docblocks that named the spec helper. The `registry.ts` import comment states the ruling and the door. Holds.
- **The pins are the right pins.** The equality table pins the identity by literal value per shape, so a resolver that moves any one row reds that row by name (ablation 1 shows it), and the dist ablation shows the protocol's own suites red when the resolver moves — so PR 2 cannot change the served answer without those suites saying so. Holds.

1. **should-fix (declaration)** — PR body line 6, `.changeset/29594-customization-pair-lookup.md` line 11, claim 6691163548: `Clause-②: no` → `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Three new re-exported names on the published `@objectstack/metadata-core` entry widen its public face by the fleet's own criterion (execution-duties.md: 公开面 = 包构建后的入口声明所达) and the precedent record 6679538573's reading of it; a wrong `no` is "可审计的假申报" (landing-operations.md). Level stays `patch`; `Metadata-protocol: none` stays; the review the `yes` owes is this record. The seat amends the claim; the dev edits the two carriers; delta review by this reviewer.
2. **should-fix (follow-up note, not this PR)** — name the six `ui/packages/app-shell` derivations (listed in ③) in the PR body's "Deferred" paragraph or on card #29594 as the `domain:ui` half's input, so the rehearsal before the ensure-door PR (HotCRM `dev:crm`, sales + 3 modules → one `app.objectstack.hotcrm.custom`) expects the console to derive `app.objectstack.hotcrm.service.custom` on its own until #29591's follow-up reads the served pair. One sentence.
